strings.d1.s0.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
strings.d1.s0.tips: The main Joseon palace. The guard-changing ceremony is at 10:00, entry is free if you wear a hanbok (rentals nearby cost 20,000 KRW), closed Tuesdays.
strings.d1.s1.name: National Folk Museum of Korea
strings.d1.s1.tips: A free folk museum inside the palace grounds.
strings.d1.s2.name: Tosokchon Samgyetang
strings.d1.s2.tips: Ginseng chicken soup next to the palace, with queues since 1983.
strings.d1.s3.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
strings.d1.s3.tips: Hanok houses and narrow lanes. Keep quiet, as people live here. There are 8 viewpoints.
strings.d1.s4.name: Insadong
strings.d1.s4.tips: Traditional crafts and tea houses, plus the Ssamziegil courtyard.
strings.d1.b0.name: Gwanghwamun Jip Kimchi Jjigae
strings.d1.b1.name: Changdeokgung Secret Garden
strings.d1.b1.tips: A UNESCO-listed palace and secret garden, visited on a timed tour. Swap it in for Bukchon.
strings.d2.s0.name: Myeongdong Shopping Street
strings.d2.s0.tips: Cosmetics and fashion, with street food stalls out in the afternoon.
strings.d2.s1.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
strings.d2.s1.tips: Kalguksu (hand-cut noodle soup) and mandu dumplings. Michelin Bib Gourmand, since 1966.
strings.d2.s2.name: Namsan Cable Car
strings.d2.s2.tips: Take the cable car up from Myeongdong, or walk up Namsan in 40 minutes.
strings.d2.s3.name: N Seoul Tower
strings.d2.s3.tips: An observation deck and love locks. Stay until 17:00 for sunset.
strings.d2.s4.name: Namdaemun Market
strings.d2.s4.tips: Korea's largest traditional market, with a hotteok (sweet filled pancake) and kalguksu alley.
strings.d2.b0.name: Isaac Toast Myeongdong
strings.d2.b1.name: Seoul Museum of Art
strings.d2.b1.tips: A free museum next to Deoksugung, good for a rainy day.
strings.d3.s0.name: Bongeunsa Temple
strings.d3.s0.tips: A Buddhist temple among the Gangnam skyscrapers, with a giant Buddha.
strings.d3.s1.name: Starfield Library COEX
strings.d3.s1.tips: 13 m bookshelves. Free, and great for photos.
strings.d3.s2.name: Gangnam Station Underground
strings.d3.s2.tips: An underground shopping arcade and K-pop shops.
strings.d3.s3.name: Samwon Garden Gangnam
strings.d3.s3.tips: Korean BBQ and galbi (marinated short ribs) since 1976, with a garden.
strings.d3.s4.name: Seonjeongneung Royal Tombs
strings.d3.s4.tips: Joseon royal tombs and woodland in the middle of the city. Peaceful.
strings.d3.b0.name: Gangnam Myeongga Galbi
strings.d3.b1.name: Lotte World Tower Seoul Sky
strings.d3.b1.tips: A 555 m observation deck with a glass floor. Swap it in for the tombs.
strings.d4.s0.name: Gyeongui Line Forest Park
strings.d4.s0.tips: A park on a former railway line, with cafes in Yeonnam-dong.
strings.d4.s1.name: Hongdae Street
strings.d4.s1.tips: A university district with street performances, vintage shops and photo booths.
strings.d4.s2.name: Hongdae Jokbal Alley
strings.d4.s2.tips: Braised pig's trotters and bossam (boiled pork wraps), served to share.
strings.d4.s3.name: Yeouido Hangang Park
strings.d4.s3.tips: A riverside walk in winter, with cafes.
strings.d4.s4.name: Han River Cruise
strings.d4.s4.tips: A sunset boat from Yeouido, with views of bridges and skyscrapers.
strings.d4.b0.name: Hongdae Andong Jjimdak
strings.d4.b1.name: 63 Building Art Museum
strings.d4.b1.tips: A golden skyscraper in Yeouido, good for a rainy day.
strings.d5.s0.name: Imjingak Park
strings.d5.s0.tips: DMZ tour (~70,000 KRW). Passport required, book 1-2 weeks ahead, no tours on Mondays. See the Freedom Bridge and the bullet-riddled train.
strings.d5.s1.name: Third Infiltration Tunnel
strings.d5.s1.tips: A tunnel dug by North Korea. It is a 350 m sloping walk, and you wear a hard hat.
strings.d5.s2.name: Dora Observatory
strings.d5.s2.tips: Look through binoculars at a North Korean village and a propaganda tower.
strings.d5.s3.name: Dorasan Station
strings.d5.s3.tips: A train station with no trains to Pyongyang.
strings.d5.s4.name: Paju Provence Village
strings.d5.s4.tips: On the way back, a cafe town themed on a French village. Stop for lunch and bakeries.
strings.d5.b0.name: Tongilchon Village Restaurant
strings.d5.b0.tips: Soybean dishes in the DMZ village.
strings.d5.b1.name: Heyri Art Village
strings.d5.b1.tips: An artists' village. Swap it in for Provence.
strings.d6.s0.name: Jogyesa Temple
strings.d6.s0.tips: The centre of Korean Buddhism, with a lantern festival in May.
strings.d6.s1.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village
strings.d6.s1.tips: Restored hanok cafes and boutiques, with the most photogenic lanes.
strings.d6.s2.name: Gwangjang Market
strings.d6.s2.tips: Bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) and mayak gimbap. The market was featured on Netflix, and you eat on stools.
strings.d6.s3.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
strings.d6.s3.tips: A restored stream in the middle of the city, with a 5 km walking path.
strings.d6.s4.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
strings.d6.s4.tips: Zaha Hadid's silver building, with exhibitions and a night market.
strings.d6.b0.name: Ikseon-dong Farm BBQ
strings.d6.b0.tips: Hanwoo (Korean beef) and Iberico BBQ in Ikseon-dong.
strings.d6.b1.name: Dongdaemun Market Night Shopping
strings.d7.s0.name: Seongsu-dong
strings.d7.s0.tips: Seoul's Brooklyn, with old factory cafes and pop-up stores.
strings.d7.s1.name: Seoul Forest
strings.d7.s1.tips: A deer park and a ginkgo path, golden yellow in autumn.
strings.d7.s2.name: Onion Seongsu
strings.d7.s2.tips: A cafe in a former factory, with pastries and coffee for a farewell treat.
strings.d7.s3.name: Seoul Station AREX
strings.d7.s3.tips: The AREX express to Incheon takes 45 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Seongsu Galbi
strings.d7.b1.name: Ttukseom Hangang Park
strings.d7.b1.tips: A riverside park, instead of the forest.
strings.note0: The T-money card works everywhere. The Climate Card gives 7 days of unlimited travel (~20,000 KRW). The AREX to Incheon takes 45 minutes, and Naver Map beats Google Maps.
strings.note1: October to November is the best season for autumn colours. Winters drop to -10°C, the palaces look beautiful in snow, the ondol (heated floor) is warm, and there are bathhouses (jjimjilbang).
strings.note2: Korean BBQ for two costs 50,000-80,000 KRW, and street food at Gwangjang is 5,000-10,000 KRW. Tipping is not expected.
strings.note3: Palaces close on Tuesdays (Gyeongbokgung) or Mondays (Changdeokgung). Entry is free in a hanbok.
strings.note4: Take your passport on the DMZ tour and book 1-2 weeks ahead. The JSA (Panmunjom) tour is separate and rarely available.
strings.note5: Cafes are part of Seoul culture: try Seongsu, Yeonnam and Ikseon-dong. Coffee costs 5,000-7,000 KRW.
strings.transit.name: T-money / Climate Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: Works on the metro and buses. The 7-day Climate Card is unlimited (~20,000 KRW).
